newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says cable will allow it to cut intl charges.
newsitem.headline: KDD says cable will allow it to cut intl charges.

text.p: Japan's biggest international telecommunications carrier, Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD), said on Thursday that a planned undersea optic fibre cable will help it further lower its international charges.

"We hope to achieve the target of cutting charges for calls to the United States to 300 yen per minute earlier than our original target year of 2000," KDD president Tadashi Nishimoto told a news conference.
KDD now charges 480 yen per minute for daytime calls.
Nishimoto said the company planned to make another rate cut by the end of this year, but that details had not been decided.
He said KDD would move into domestic call services after a law restricting its business to international services was amended.
Such an amendment is expected to be made by next summer.
"We will do what we can do using our own facilities next year," Nishimoto said.
The new undersea cable could be used for domestic long-distance calls as well as data communications, he said.
Nishimoto said the cable would allow KDD to cut its yearly access payments to NTT by 10 billion yen from the current 30 billion yen.
Because the access payments to NTT were expected to go up drastically when KDD moved into local services, KDD decided to construct its own low-cost network using the undersea cable.
KDD said earlier on Thursday it would invest 100 billion yen to lay the cable by 1999.
Nishimoto said because it was cheaper to lay the cable under the sea than on land, KDD would be able to offer domestic long-distance call services cheaper than NTT.
KDD said in a statement that the 8,500 km cable would loop around three of Japan's main islands. It is expected to be in use by mid-1999.
